## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design high-throughput native modules with tight JS<->native coupling and GPU rendering. It probes multi-threading, memory management, and hardware-accelerated rendering choices across iOS and Android.

## Key Concepts
- TurboModule/JSI bridge and async queues
- Metal/Vulkan/OpenGL interoperability
- ringbuffer, triple buffering, lock-free structures
- backpressure, memory management, GC interaction
- thermal/power diagnostics and on-device testing

## Code Example
```javascript
// Minimal API sketch
initChart(800,600,{capacity:1000000});
pushBatch(points); // array of {x,y} with fixed-point encoding
onFrame(() => { /* render-ready callback */ });
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you calibrate backpressure thresholds for bursty data?
- What strategies would you use to verify performance across devices with different GPUs?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a cross-platform RN native module that performs real-time on-device ML inference, bridging frames from the camera to a GPU-accelerated model, with careful backpressure, lifecycle, and privacy considerations.

## Key Concepts
- RN native modules: TurboModules/JSI bridging for cross-platform APIs
- On-device ML: GPU acceleration (Metal on iOS, Vulkan/NNAPI on Android)
- Concurrency: dedicated frame producer thread, GPU worker, bounded frame/detection queues
- Backpressure: drop or throttle frames to avoid JS backlog while keeping UI responsive
- Lifecycle: clean shutdown, model swap without leaks, pause/resume semantics

## Code Example
```javascript
// Implementation sketch (pseudo)
RNDetector.startDetection(modelPath, {fps:15})
RNDetector.onDetections((detections) => handleDetections(detections))
RNDetector.switchModel(newModelPath)
RNDetector.pause()
RNDetector.resume()
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you measure and bound memory usage across devices with different GPUs?
- How would you secure data privacy if the model occasionally uses cloud fallback?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests offline-first reasoning, caching strategy, and small React hooks. It maps to real-world data resilience needs in consumer apps.

## Key Concepts
- Offline-first data layer
- TTL-based caching with async storage
- Background refresh and cache invalidation
- Lightweight bridge API and small React hook
- Online/offline detection (NetInfo) for revalidation

## Code Example
```javascript
function useOfflineQuery(key, fetcher, ttl) {
  // skeleton
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle cache size growth?
- How would you test offline behavior end-to-end?
